import os
import smtplib

from platform_config import http_timeout

SMTP_HOST = "smtp.harbourbikes.example"
SMTP_USER = "notifications"


def send_email(message):
    server = smtplib.SMTP(SMTP_HOST, 587, timeout=http_timeout("notifications"))

    server.login(SMTP_USER, os.environ["SMTP_PASSWORD"])
    server.send_message(message)
    server.quit()

"""Email sending for booking confirmations, receipts and reminders; Celery tasks call send_email."""

import os
import smtplib

from platform_config import http_timeout

SMTP_HOST = "smtp.harbourbikes.example"
SMTP_USER = "notifications"


def send_email(message):
    server = smtplib.SMTP(SMTP_HOST, 587, timeout=http_timeout("notifications"))
    server.starttls()
    server.login(SMTP_USER, os.environ["SMTP_PASSWORD"])
    server.send_message(message)
    server.quit()

"""Email sending for booking confirmations, receipts and reminders; Celery tasks call send_email."""

import os
import smtplib

from platform_config import http_timeout

SMTP_HOST = "smtp.harbourbikes.example"
SMTP_USER = "notifications"


def send_email(message):
    server = smtplib.SMTP(SMTP_HOST, 587, timeout=http_timeout("notifications"))
    server.starttls()
    server.login(SMTP_USER, os.environ["SMTP_PASSWORD"])
    server.send_message(message)
    server.quit()

import smtplib

from platform_config import http_timeout

SMTP_HOST = "smtp.harbourbikes.example"

"""Email sending for booking confirmations, receipts and reminders; Celery tasks call send_email."""

import os
import smtplib

from platform_config import http_timeout

SMTP_HOST = "smtp.harbourbikes.example"
SMTP_USER = "notifications"


def send_email(message):
    server = smtplib.SMTP(SMTP_HOST, 587, timeout=http_timeout("notifications"))
    server.starttls()
    server.login(SMTP_USER, os.environ["SMTP_PASSWORD"])
    server.send_message(message)
    server.quit()

import smtplib

from platform_config import http_timeout

SMTP_HOST = "smtp.harbourbikes.example"
SMTP_USER = "notifications"


def send_email(message):
    server = smtplib.SMTP(SMTP_HOST, 587, timeout=http_timeout("notifications"))
    server.starttls()
    server.login(SMTP_USER, os.environ["SMTP_PASSWORD"])
    server.send_message(message)
    server.quit()

hub_requests.reason: notifications needs smtp_timeout 2s-20s (relay greets in up to 1.5s); the 300ms default would break SMTP. Please grant a notifications override of 5s.

workers.notes: Added timeout=http_timeout("notifications") to the SMTP connection, which is the outbound call in send_email. Pinned all requirements. The effective timeout is 300ms until the lead grants an override, which is below the 2s minimum need, so I requested 5s via hub_changes. I did not write overrides myself. The SMTP password is already read from the environment, and the owner is set.

name: customer-profiles
description: Stores customer accounts (name, email, phone, driving-licence check, saved payment method token).
owner:
  team: Team Identity
  contact: identity@harbourbikes.example

overrides: {}

workers.notes: The profiles-db Postgres sits on a VM local disk and inherited backup.policy 'none', so customer data had no backup. I set backup to daily/30d in service.yaml. files.fleet-telemetry/service.yaml:
name: fleet-telemetry
description: Ingests GPS position and battery level from every bike over MQTT, writes to TimescaleDB, alerts on bikes leaving the city.
owner: {team: Team Fleet, contact: fleet@harbourbikes.example}
runtime: rust (tokio)
instances: 2  # raised from 1 so a single VM or process failure no longer stops ingest
zones: 1
data:
  store: managed TimescaleDB (point-in-time recovery, 7 days)
  location: managed
backup: null  # not needed: data is in the managed database (point-in-time recovery)
notes: If the VM is down, bikes buffer 15 minutes of readings, then drop them.

workers.notes: Set owner to Team Fleet (was null). Raised instances from 1 to 2 to remove the single point of failure. Removed the empty overrides block. Backup stays null because the data is in managed TimescaleDB with PITR. Cargo dependencies are already pinned exactly. main.rs has no secrets or outbound HTTP calls. Remaining risk: the Mosquitto broker still shares the telemetry-01 VM, and moving it needs infrastructure work outside these files.

files.maintenance-scheduler/service.yaml:
name: maintenance-scheduler
description: Nightly at 02:00 plans the next day's repair routes from mileage and fault reports; the mechanics' tablets download the plan at 06:00.
owner:
  team: Team Fleet
  contact: fleet@harbourbikes.example
runtime: python3.11 (cron)
instances: 1  # one crontab entry on ops-cron-01; nothing alerts if the job does not run
zones: 1
data:
  store: SQLite files plan.sqlite and history.sqlite (three years of repair records)
  location: vm-local-disk
backup: daily/30d  # platform backup job copies the VM-local SQLite files to object storage

workers.notes: Fixed the unbacked-up data on VM-local disk: backup set from null (inherits none) to daily/30d, covering the three years of repair history. Removed the empty overrides block since services may not write it. Dependencies are already pinned, there is no outbound HTTP or secret in the code, and the owner is valid. instances stays 1 because the job writes local SQLite files and running it on two instances would conflict. The missing alert when the cron job does not run cannot be fixed within these rules.

import smtplib

from platform_config import http_timeout

SMTP_HOST = "smtp.harbourbikes.example"

import os
import smtplib

from platform_config import http_timeout

SMTP_HOST = "smtp.harbourbikes.example"

"""Email sending for booking confirmations, receipts and reminders; Celery tasks call send_email."""

import os
import smtplib

from platform_config import http_timeout

SMTP_HOST = "smtp.harbourbikes.example"
SMTP_USER = "notifications"


def send_email(message):
    server = smtplib.SMTP(SMTP_HOST, 587, timeout=http_timeout("notifications"))
    server.starttls()
    server.login(SMTP_USER, os.environ["SMTP_PASSWORD"])
    server.send_message(message)
    server.quit()
